title: A restore asks for its database before it stops the site or swaps the webroot
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout run: node --test --test-reporter=tap packages/fleet/tracy-fleet-operation/test/db-ready.test.mjs

S2: Record the exit code, the '# tests', '# pass', '# fail' lines and the result of each case whose name starts with: "restore: a database that never comes up stops the restore before the site is touched".
expect: S1 exits 0 with '# fail 0' and '# pass' equal to '# tests' (at least 8).

Every named case is 'ok' (none 'not ok', none '# SKIP'): restore.sh starts the db service and waits for it ('==> checking the database') right after the snapshot is fetched and DB_PASSWORD read; a database that never comes up ends the run there, before the web container is stopped, the webroot replaced or the image changed.
evidence: Review of the L13 fix, 05/10/2026: restore.sh waited for the database only at step 5, after step 2 had stopped the web container, step 3 replaced the webroot and step 4 changed the image, so a database that never came up (a password the volume does not know, a server that will not start) left a half-restored site serving nothing. Red d77ed59de, fix 7a21045f0.
fence: A restore that cannot reach its database changes nothing on the site and says why; step 5 still waits again before the DROP.

tests: restore: a database that never comes up stops the restore before the site is touched
